00:00 - Maya Patel: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. uh quick roll call from our side, diego and i are on.
00:10 - Ellen Brooks: hi this is ellen, samir here as well, jade and tom on our side.

00:41 - Tom Hsu: procurement question up front — we'd like to avoid multi-month price surprises. need clear escalation path on overages.
00:50 - Maya Patel: totally understood. we'll propose tiered commit with defined burst buckets and overage caps, also an escalation SLA. i'll share a draft after.
01:02 - Diego Ramos: quick tech note — burst behavior depends on whether you go hosted vs dedicated GPU pools. dedicated gives stronger throughput guarantees, hosted is more elastic but variable latency.
01:18 - Jade Nguyen: can you define "burst buckets" — like how are bursts charged and can we reserve them?
01:25 - Maya Patel: yes, so think of a baseline commit that's reserved, then a burst allowance that can be used month-to-month. bursts priced at a stepped rate. optional auto-burst with early-notify to procurement is possible.
01:38 - Samir Patel: what about private nodes in eu? our compliance team needs data never leave eu region.
01:45 - Diego Ramos: private deployment (VPC) can be pinned to eu regions, with local KMS keys — we integrate with customer KMS (okta of sorts? i mean AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault) — apologies, sounded garbled there.
01:58 - Ellen Brooks: we need SOC2 + ISO attestation for the private plane and audit logs. what level of log retention?
02:08 - Maya Patel: standard audit logs 90 days in the console, enterprise add-on for 12 months retention. for private we can ship logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder.
02:19 - Tom Hsu: that's good. does that add cost?
02:22 - Maya Patel: the long-retention is an add-on; we'll show line item in the contract amendment.
02:28 - Speaker 1: (crosstalk)
02:35 - Diego Ramos: i want to call out latency profiles — if you're running at 512 token average sequences, we can usually hit sub-120ms p95 on dedicated with our optimized kernels. on hosted the p95 could move to 150–250ms depending on load.
02:52 - Jade Nguyen: hmm our product needs sub-200ms p95 for chat, and higher-throughput for batch ranking overnight.
03:01 - Diego Ramos: right, so hybrid makes sense: dedicated for low-latency chat endpoints, hosted for asynchronous batch jobs. caching and prefix-KV caching for repeated prompts will reduce cost.
03:16 - Ellen Brooks: any concerns with quantization and quality? our NLP team is picky about hallucination drift.
03:23 - Diego Ramos: quantization to int8 or int4 generally reduces cost but tuning is required. we can run a quality regression against your prompt set in the pilot. we recommend int8 first and eval on a holdout prompts set.
03:38 - Samir Patel: ok good. pricing tradeoffs are clear. question: can we see a 12-month forecast built into the amendment with quarterly top-ups?
03:47 - Maya Patel: yes, that's the cadence we're proposing — baseline monthly commit with a quarterly checkpoint to roll capacity up or down with 30 days notice.
03:56 - Tom Hsu: any minimum commitment length?
03:59 - Maya Patel: contract change would be a 12-month commitment for the baseline, with flexible add-on bursts. the amendment will include early-exit terms and pro-rated refunds for downsizing.
04:12 - Jade Nguyen: on private deployment — network egress is a big one. we need to know if you require outbound access to specific control plane endpoints.
04:20 - Diego Ramos: for private we offer two modes: private control plane (where control plane traffic goes over an established peering) or fully air-gapped with manual package installs. both support customer KMS. peering needs a limited set of endpoints, we'll share the CIDR list.
04:36 - Ellen Brooks: and the HSM/KMS — can we keep keys in our HSM?
04:40 - Diego Ramos: yes with HSM integration (bring-your-own-HSM) we can wrap keys; we'll coordinate with your security team on the certs.
04:49 - Samir Patel: we want to run a perf benchmark before committing — 1k concurrent streams, 512 token average, and measure p50/p95, throughput and error rates. can you do that?
04:59 - Diego Ramos: absolutely. i'll run it on a staging cluster that mirrors your dedicated profile. i'll capture token-level traces and KV cache hit patterns.
05:11 - Maya Patel: diego will send the benchmark plan and template results file. ellen, can you send the prompt sets?
05:17 - Ellen Brooks: yes i'll share via the secure bucket — but note some prompts are PII-ish, we'll sanitize first.
05:25 - Tom Hsu: procurement also wants a clear overage notification workflow — ideally email and webhook to our cost center.
05:32 - Maya Patel: we have webhook hooks and cost alerts; we'll include a runbook in the amendment.
05:38 - Speaker 2: (brief pause)
05:45 - Diego Ramos: technical deep-dive — autoscaling policy options: predictive based on time-of-day QPS, reactive with target CPU/GPU util, and hybrid using prefix cache hit metrics to avoid spinning up nodes for cache-friendly workloads.
06:02 - Jade Nguyen: predictive sounds useful. our traffic is e-comm flash sale heavy; predictability is low.
06:10 - Diego Ramos: then i'd recommend baseline dedicated for the steady chat load and hosted bursting for flash spikes; combined with a cold-cache warm-up strategy.
06:19 - Samir Patel: is there any vendor lock if we use the private deployment?
06:23 - Maya Patel: no vendor lock — you can export models and KV caches, and we provide tooling to migrate workloads. private nodes use standard container images and infra templates.
06:34 - Ellen Brooks: regarding observability — we'll need token-level cost breakdowns mapped to our internal product ids. is that available?
06:42 - Maya Patel: yes per-route and per-token breakdowns with tagging, you'll get a console view plus csv export for your billing system.
06:50 - Tom Hsu: timeline — what's a realistic pilot to full onboarding plan?
06:54 - Diego Ramos: pilot (2 weeks) for perf + quality tests, then a 3–4 week private node setup and config, so end-to-end maybe 6–8 weeks to production if no blockers.
07:07 - Samir Patel: ok that feels reasonable. what about DR and fallback — if private nodes fail does traffic route to hosted?
07:14 - Diego Ramos: yes automatic fallback policy can route to a compatible hosted model variant. you can set cost/latency thresholds for auto-fallback.
07:24 - Jade Nguyen: we need to test that failover path in the pilot.
07:27 - Diego Ramos: agreed, we'll include failover tests in the benchmark plan.
07:33 - Ellen Brooks: any SOC2 or penetration test windows required by you for private?
07:38 - Maya Patel: we can share our SOC2 report and run joint pen tests; for private we support customer-led pentests with a short notification window.
07:48 - Tom Hsu: procurement will want indemnity language for data breach, is that on the table?
07:53 - Maya Patel: yes we can surface standard enterprise indemnity clauses; legal will follow up.
07:59 - Speaker 1: (chuckle)
08:05 - Samir Patel: curious about model variants — do you offer quantized variants we can use only for lower-criticality flows?
08:11 - Diego Ramos: yes model variants with different quantization/precision profiles are supported, and routing policies can split traffic by route.
08:18 - Jade Nguyen: nice — that helps with cost segregation.
08:22 - Ellen Brooks: what's the SLA for dedicated nodes?
08:26 - Maya Patel: dedicated SLA is 99.9% uptime with latency targets baked in; exact numbers depend on tier in the contract.
08:33 - Tom Hsu: we'll want that spelled out.
08:36 - Maya Patel: noted. i'll add SLA table to the amendment.
08:41 - Diego Ramos: one more perf nuance — KV cache hit rate is the single biggest lever for cost. if you can structure prompts with stable prefixes we often see 20–40% token savings.
08:53 - Samir Patel: we should run a quick tokenization analysis against our most common prompts.
08:58 - Ellen Brooks: i'll have my team run that and share results.
09:04 - Maya Patel: perfect. next — pricing scenario walk-through. i'll show three scenarios: conservative, expected, and aggressive commit.
09:12 - Speaker 3: (low audio)
09:18 - Maya Patel: conservative keeps baseline low and uses hosted bursts; expected uses modest dedicated for chat; aggressive reserves more dedicated capacity for peak reliability.
09:29 - Tom Hsu: financially we'd prefer to keep baseline lower and pay for bursts, but need caps.
09:34 - Maya Patel: doable — the amendment will have a burst cap and auto-notify thresholds.
09:40 - Jade Nguyen: any additional work for our infra team for private?
09:44 - Diego Ramos: minimal — peer setup, a small set of network rules, and KMS integration. we'll provide terraform templates.
09:51 - Samir Patel: terraform templates are a must.
09:53 - Diego Ramos: absolutely, we'll share.

10:38 - Diego Ramos: maintenance windows are customer-configurable; we recommend low-traffic windows and optional 24/7 support add-on if you need zero-touch upgrades.
10:48 - Ellen Brooks: security question — do you allow bringing our own model weights? we sometimes train in-house and want to serve them.
10:54 - Diego Ramos: yes BYOM supported on private with appropriate model onboarding checks and a signing process.
11:02 - Samir Patel: that helps our roadmap.

11:12 - Ellen Brooks: perf numbers, legal indemnities, and security attestation.
11:16 - Tom Hsu: and procurement needs cost certainty in the amendment.
